newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Barak far ahead of Netanyahu in poll.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Barak far ahead of Netanyahu in poll.

text.p: An opinion poll released on Friday showed opposition Labour leader Ehud Barak would crush Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu by a margin of nearly two to one, were elections to be held this week.
Netanyahu's ruling coalition has been shaken by internal disputes, most recently a conflict in which the prime minister forced the resignation of Dan Meridor as finance minister.
The Dahaf Institute poll, conducted on Thursday, showed Barak would defeat Netanyahu by a margin of 51 percent to 26.
Israeli general elections are scheduled for the year 2000, but a vote could come sooner if Netanyahu's slim six-vote majority in the 120-seat parliament should unravel.

Ex-army chief Barak took over the Labour leadership from Shimon Peres early this month, defeating three challengers in an internal party election. Netanyahu beat Peres in an upset victory in May 1996 elections.
Polls have shown Barak gaining steadily on Netanyahu since last month, when the two were neck-and-neck.
